title: The infrastructure for tokenized bank deposits is beginning to take shape
gist: Tokenized bank deposits are breaking out of proprietary bank blockchains as SWIFT launches a shared ledger with seventeen banks, BIS Project Agora completes $1 million of real-value cross-border tests with twenty-eight institutions, and the Clearing House pilots on-chain netting that settles residuals in Fed reserves. With FDIC confirming deposit insurance eligibility and Citigroup projecting over $100 trillion of annual tokenized-deposit turnover by 2030, the wholesale rails are forming alongside — not against — the $33 trillion stablecoin market.

insights.claim: SWIFT launched a blockchain-based shared ledger this month with seventeen banks from six continents piloting live transactions, marking a major step toward 24/7 cross-border payments with tokenized bank deposits.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: SWIFT moving from messaging to an orchestration ledger defends its cross-border franchise and defines the standard rail banks will build to.
insights.locator: Just this month, the Society for Worldwide Interbank Financial Telecommunication

insights.claim: Project Agora, led by the Bank for International Settlements with seven central banks, announced that twenty-eight financial institutions and central banks across Asia, Europe, and North America completed seventeen real-value transaction scenarios totaling approximately $1 million on a shared platform for tokenized commercial bank deposits and central bank money.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Real-value (not simulated) settlement on a unified public-private ledger is the technical proof point; the $1 million size shows it is still pilot-scale.
insights.locator: Meanwhile, Project Agora, led by the Bank for International Settlements

insights.claim: Tokenized bank deposits have until now largely remained confined to proprietary bank networks, limiting their use across institutions and jurisdictions, especially compared with stablecoins whose transaction volume reached $33 trillion in 2025.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Anchors the scale gap: stablecoins already clear $33tn a year while bank tokenized deposits are siloed — interoperability is the variable that closes it.
insights.locator: Until now, these deposits have largely remained confined

themes.theme: US issuers and the Clearing House netting layer

insights.claim: JPMorgan Chase, the largest issuer of tokenized deposits, has processed more than $7 billion in transactions daily with cumulative volume of more than $4 trillion to date using its Kinexys network, formerly Onyx.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: JPMorgan already runs the largest live tokenized-deposit franchise — a concrete lead in wholesale on-chain settlement that peers must replicate or join.
insights.locator: In the US, the largest issuer of tokenized deposits

insights.claim: Bank of New York Mellon is enabling tokenized deposits via its private permissioned blockchain for on-chain bank-to-bank settlement, and the Texas Bankers Association with San Antonio-based Vantage Bank announced an Innovation Magnet Program giving member banks structured access to tokenized deposit technology.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Adoption is spreading past money-center banks to regional and community bank consortia, broadening the vendor and infrastructure addressable market.
insights.locator: Meanwhile, the Bank of New York Mellon (BNY)

insights.claim: The Clearing House launched a pilot on-chain clearing and settlement system for tokenized deposits that nets transactions among international banks and links blockchain transactions directly to the Real-Time Payments network and CHIPS, with residual imbalances after netting cleared and settled in reserves at the Federal Reserve's core ledger.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Settling residuals in Fed reserves gives tokenized deposits central-bank-money finality — the structural feature stablecoins cannot match.
insights.locator: As part of efforts to overcome fragmentation

insights.claim: In the European Union, discussion has focused on the European Central Bank providing a trusted public anchor or wholesale bridge to allow cross-bank convertibility and interoperability between distributed ledger platforms and the TARGET payment system.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: The EU model routes interoperability through the central bank rather than private consortia — a different control structure with different vendor winners.
insights.locator: In the European Union, discussion has focused

insights.claim: Hong Kong's Project Ensemble provides a regulatory sandbox for wholesale CBDCs and tokenized deposits while Singapore's Project Guardian tests asset tokenization across fixed-income, foreign exchange, and asset management in a cross-border sandbox.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Asian financial centers are competing on sandbox breadth; early standards set there will shape where tokenized asset issuance domiciles.
insights.locator: In Hong Kong, Project Ensemble has provided a regulatory sandbox

insights.claim: China's CBDC, the e-CNY, is moving toward a tokenized deposit system that allows wallet balances to earn interest.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: An interest-bearing retail CBDC blurs the line with bank deposits and would be a disintermediation risk template other central banks watch closely.

themes.theme: Regulation tilting the field toward deposits

insights.claim: The FDIC clarified that it is technologically neutral about how deposit records are maintained — traditional bank books or distributed ledger including blockchain — so tokenized bank deposits are fully eligible for deposit insurance and can earn interest.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Insured plus interest-bearing is a decisive product advantage over stablecoins for corporate cash — the key regulatory unlock for treasury adoption.
insights.locator: Rules are starting to catch up with technology

insights.claim: Federal Reserve Governor Michael Barr has said that tokenized deposits are more robust than stablecoins, as tokenized deposits are treated as part of banks' normal operations subject to applicable regulatory and supervisory oversight.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Explicit Fed-governor preference signals which instrument regulators will favor in wholesale settlement — relevant to stablecoin issuers' institutional TAM.
insights.locator: As a result, Fed Governor Michael Barr has said

insights.claim: The proposed Clarity Act could favor tokenized deposits by restricting stablecoin rewards, with limited exceptions for activity-based rewards linked to transactions, payments, and loyalty programs rather than passive holding.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: A yield ban on passive stablecoin holding while insured tokenized deposits pay interest would redirect institutional balances toward banks — a direct legislative catalyst.
insights.locator: Meanwhile, there has been some progress in the legislative process

themes.theme: Live use cases: treasury, DvP, and programmable trade finance

insights.claim: Corporate treasurers are actively using tokenized deposits to manage cross-border liquidity, benefiting from instant clearing and settlement while avoiding traditional SWIFT messaging and correspondent banks, significantly reducing transaction costs.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Correspondent banking fee income is the revenue pool being disintermediated; banks with tokenized rails capture it, laggards lose it.
insights.locator: Tokenized deposits move from theory to practice

insights.claim: Delivery-versus-payment becomes instantaneous when tokenized bank deposits pay for tokenized assets, reducing the counterparty settlement risk that arises from T+1 or T+2 settlement periods.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Atomic DvP collapses settlement risk and the collateral/margin buffers held against it — a balance-sheet efficiency gain for dealers and clearers.
insights.locator: In particular, delivery-versus-payment can become instantaneous

insights.claim: Programmability lets banks embed smart contracts in financial flows that trigger payments when performance benchmarks are met by participants in a transaction chain, as in trade finance, reducing reliance on paper-based documentation and telex and fax communications.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Trade finance is the highest-friction target for programmable money; digitizing it is a cost-take-out opportunity for banks still running telex and fax.
insights.locator: The programmability of tokenized deposits

themes.theme: Sizing the 2030 opportunity and the deposit/stablecoin division of labor

insights.claim: Citigroup estimates that by 2030 the annual turnover volume of tokenized deposits could exceed $100 trillion, matching its projected volume for stablecoins.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: A $100tn/yr turnover forecast implies enormous infrastructure and custody fee pools; test it against the current ~$4tn cumulative JPMorgan base.
insights.locator: A market poised for growth

insights.claim: Tokenized real-world assets have reached between $30 billion and $36 billion in value, including $15 billion in US Treasury securities, $7.3 billion in commodities, $1.5 billion in stocks, plus growing private credit and real estate, and Citigroup forecasts total tokenized assets ballooning to between $5.5 trillion and $8.2 trillion by 2030.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Current RWA base of $30-36bn against a $5.5-8.2tn 2030 forecast implies a ~200x expansion — a specific, falsifiable growth assumption to track quarterly.
insights.locator: Fundamentally, the growth of tokenized deposits is integral

insights.claim: Tokenized deposits and stablecoins are complementary rather than substitutes: tokenized deposits serve wholesale activity including cross-border treasury operations and tokenized asset transactions, while dollar stablecoins dominate remittances and emerging markets where they hedge unstable domestic monetary conditions.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Segments the market so investors avoid a false either/or: wholesale bank rails and retail dollar-access stablecoins can both scale.
insights.locator: It is important to note that tokenized deposits and stablecoins

insights.claim: Stablecoins, especially those originating outside the United States, also feature in illicit transactions according to the Financial Action Task Force.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Offshore stablecoin issuers carry a distinct AML/regulatory tail risk that US-regulated tokenized deposits do not.
insights.locator: Stablecoins, especially those originating outside the US

insights.claim: Tokenized deposits, stablecoins, and wholesale CBDCs will eventually coexist, and their adoption and impact will depend on whether commercial banks, central banks, regulators, and infrastructure providers can build interoperable systems that make cross-border payments faster and safer.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Interoperability standards, not any single instrument's technology, are the gating variable — watch consortium and central-bank bridge announcements.
insights.quote: The technology remains in its early stages, but the foundations are taking shape.
insights.locator: Tokenized deposits, stablecoins, and wholesale CBDCs will one day coexist

insights.claim: Financial Stability Board Secretary General John Schindler argued in a speech at the Atlantic Council that international coordination remains essential in finance because risks and innovation do not stop at national borders.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: FSB attention to cross-border tokenization signals a coming international standards workstream that could constrain fragmented national approaches.
insights.locator: In a speech at the Atlantic Council earlier this week
